title: Pythagoras and Trigonometry in 3D
standard_text: Apply Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometric ratios to find angles and lengths in right-angled triangles in three-dimensional figures.
meta_desc: Free Year 11 GCSE maths worksheets on lengths of diagonals and angles between lines and planes in cuboids and pyramids. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Find a right-angled triangle inside the solid and draw it flat.
key_sub: Space diagonal = √(l² + w² + h²); a pyramid's apex is above the centre of its base.
body_html:
How it works

  • Find a right-angled triangle inside the solid and draw it flat. Most 3D problems need two triangles: one on the base and one standing up.
  • Space diagonal of a cuboid = √(l² + w² + h²).
  • The angle between a line and a plane is the angle between the line and its projection (shadow) on the plane.
  • In a right pyramid, the apex is directly above the centre of the base, so use half the base diagonal.
Example

A cuboid is 8 cm by 6 cm by 5 cm. Find the angle between the space diagonal and the base.

Base diagonal = √(8² + 6²) = 10

tan θ = 5 ÷ 10

Answer: 26.6°

Example

A right pyramid has a square base of side 10 cm and height 12 cm. Find the slant edge.

Half the base diagonal = √50 = 7.07 cm

√(12² + 7.07²)

Answer: 13.9 cm

Common mistakes

  • Using a face diagonal instead of the space diagonal.
  • Using the whole base diagonal instead of half of it for a pyramid.
  • Measuring the angle with the vertical instead of with the plane.
  • Forgetting to find the base length first in 3D elevation problems.

faq.q: How do you solve 3D trigonometry problems?
faq.a: Identify a right-angled triangle that contains the length or angle you need, draw it in 2D, and use Pythagoras' theorem or SOH CAH TOA. You may need to find a side from another triangle first.

faq.q: What is the angle between a line and a plane?
faq.a: Drop a perpendicular from the top of the line to the plane. The angle is between the line and the line joining its foot to the point where the line meets the plane.

faq.q: How do you find the space diagonal of a cuboid?
faq.a: Use √(l² + w² + h²): first the base diagonal √(l² + w²), then Pythagoras again with the height.

faq.q: Why do pyramid problems use half the base diagonal?
faq.a: The apex of a right pyramid is directly above the centre of the base, and the centre is halfway along each diagonal.
